AgentGateway.title: AgentGateway

CapabilitiesMessage.description: What this route offers. The library probes; the host caches (§9.4).
CapabilitiesMessage.title: CapabilitiesMessage

ConfigField.description: One control the host draws, and one value it sends back.
ConfigField.title: ConfigField

Denial.description: One call the host's policy refused, and why.
Denial.title: Denial

DescribeMessage.description: What SDKs are real, and what gateway kinds can be configured (§10).
DescribeMessage.title: DescribeMessage

Diff.description:
A change to one file, as the change itself rather than as a tool call.

`before = None` is a whole new file: there is no old text, and a host draws
only additions. `before = ""` is an edit whose old text was empty, which is
a different thing and draws one empty removed line.
Diff.title: Diff

ErrorEvent.description:
The run failed, and this is what it said.

A failed turn still costs money and still took time, so both are carried:
a host that draws a cost on the row would otherwise show nothing for the one
kind of run whose cost is most worth seeing.
ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent

EventMessage.description: One thing happened in a run (§7).
EventMessage.title: EventMessage

FieldError.description: One answer the reviewer must fix before the gateway can be saved.
FieldError.title: FieldError

GatewayRoute.description:
How one SDK reaches one gateway.

A gateway holds one route **per SDK**, because the base URL is a function of
the gateway *and* the SDK: each SDK speaks a different wire protocol, and a
gateway serves each protocol at a different path. A gateway with no route
for an SDK does not offer that SDK.
GatewayRoute.title: GatewayRoute

KindDescriptor.description: One gateway kind: what to ask the reviewer, and what each SDK gets.
KindDescriptor.title: KindDescriptor

LogMessage.description: A line for the host's log. **Never a credential** (§4.4).
LogMessage.title: LogMessage

ModelChoice.description: One row of a model picker, named by the adapter that knows the SDK.
ModelChoice.title: ModelChoice

NewSession.description: Start a session and let the SDK name it. The id comes back in `RunResult`.
NewSession.title: NewSession

PolicyMessage.description:
Judge this tool call before it runs (§8).

**No answer within thirty seconds is a deny.** A policy the host does not
answer is a bug in the host, and a bug in the host must never become a write.
PolicyMessage.title: PolicyMessage

PolicyReplyMessage.description: The host's answer about one tool call. None allows; a string refuses.
PolicyReplyMessage.title: PolicyReplyMessage

ReadyMessage.description: The loop is up. Sent once, first, and it is the only health check there is.
ReadyMessage.title: ReadyMessage

ResolvedRoute.description: §5.3 — what a run is actually given. Built by the host, never stored here.
ResolvedRoute.title: ResolvedRoute

ResultMessage.description: The run is over. Nothing more will arrive for this `run_id`.
ResultMessage.title: ResultMessage

ResumeSession.description: Continue the session this id names.
ResumeSession.title: ResumeSession

RouteCapabilities.description:
What this SDK, through this gateway, can actually offer.

`error` is not a failure of the probe's caller: a route that cannot be asked
still has to render, and a host draws the sentence rather than an empty
picker.
RouteCapabilities.title: RouteCapabilities

RouteNote.description:
What one kind offers one SDK — described, and as a template.

`protocol` and `note` are for the host to show. The three template fields
are how `build_routes()` turns the reviewer's answers into a `GatewayRoute`:
a `{key}` in `base_url` or `credential_env` is replaced by the value of the
field with that key, or by that field's `default` when the host sent none.

**A template that resolves to nothing offers no route.** `base_url=None`
means "this SDK uses its own endpoint" — the `original` kind — and is a
route. `base_url="{claudeUrl}"` with no `claudeUrl` answered means the
reviewer did not configure this SDK, and `build_routes()` leaves it out
rather than inventing a gateway that addresses nothing.
RouteNote.title: RouteNote

RunMessage.description:
Start a run. **It has no reply**: its acknowledgement is its first event,
and its completion is its `result`.
RunMessage.title: RunMessage

RunRequest.description:
Everything a run needs, and nothing that names an SDK.

Three inputs are named for what they MEAN rather than for what one SDK calls
them, and that is the whole difference between this and an SDK call:

* `system_prompt` is text. How an adapter installs it is its own business.
* `disallowed` is a list of common tools. The adapter turns them into its
  SDK's own names.
* `plugins` are absolute directories, opaque here. The adapter wraps them in
  whatever shape its SDK wants, and refuses them if it has no such shape.
RunRequest.title: RunRequest

RunResult.description: The run is over. Nothing more will arrive for this `run_id`.
RunResult.title: RunResult

SdkDescriptor.description: One SDK a host may offer. Only SDKs with an adapter are listed.
SdkDescriptor.title: SdkDescriptor

SeedSession.description: Start a session, and use this id. The host computed it and will store it.
SeedSession.title: SeedSession

SessionExistsMessage.description: Whether the SDK can still resume this session (§9.3).
SessionExistsMessage.title: SessionExistsMessage

SessionState.description:
What the SDK knows about one session, and what is on disk for it.

The record and the file are reported **separately**, and that separation is
the point: they can disagree, and every way they disagree is a different
bug. A record with no file means the store moved. A file with no record
means the SDK will refuse to resume it and the host's own replay is what
will actually happen. Collapsing the two into one "resumable: yes" is what
hid both.
SessionState.title: SessionState

ShutdownMessage.description: Finish the open runs and exit 0.
ShutdownMessage.title: ShutdownMessage

Started.description:
The SDK is up, and these are the values it RESOLVED.

Not what the host asked for — what the SDK will actually use, so a
disagreement shows up as a disagreement rather than as a silent pass.
Started.title: Started

StopMessage.description: End this run. It finishes with a `stopped` event and a `result`.
StopMessage.title: StopMessage

StoppedEvent.description:
A person ended this run. Never a fault, and never an error.

It carries what the run had spent when it was ended, for the same reason
`ErrorEvent` does.
StoppedEvent.title: StoppedEvent

ToolCall.description: One tool call, on its way to the host's policy.
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

VerifyMessage.description:
Spec 43 §2.4 — what this server publishes, checked against this route.

**It writes nothing and returns no URL.** Discovery verifies a judgement
already made in `catalogue.py`; it never makes one.
VerifyMessage.title: VerifyMessage

VerifyResult.description: What one server said about itself, and whether it named this route's path.
VerifyResult.title: VerifyResult

Wrote.description: A write tool named this path. The primary source for "what did this touch".
Wrote.title: Wrote
